title: [Q6] Decide virtual-table versus dedicated resumable graph cursor
description:
Measure worst-case work before first output, cancellation latency, fairness, and memory. Retain the virtual-table adapter or replace it with a dedicated yield-safe graph cursor/opcode based on evidence.

## Rationale

The existing virtual-table scan path minimizes core changes, but its synchronous cursor contract may not provide bounded cooperative execution for expensive shortest-path searches. The decision must be driven by measured latency and fairness.

## Alternatives Considered

1. Retain the internal virtual-table adapter when each call has bounded work and cancellation latency.
2. Add a dedicated resumable graph cursor/opcode when explicit yield-safe state is required.
3. Reject widening every internal virtual-table cursor to asynchronous I/O solely for graph traversal.
acceptance_criteria: Decision and measurements are recorded; chosen adapter passes cancellation/resource tests; any core state machine has deterministic yield, resume, and abandonment coverage.

title: [D4] Decide and implement derived-state persistence mode
description:
Measure rebuild, startup, memory, write, and refresh costs; retain in-memory rebuild if sufficient, otherwise implement same-file versioned internal chunks with atomic publish. A sidecar requires a separate product decision.

## Rationale

CSR state is derived and must remain recoverable without weakening Turso's one-file or transaction guarantees. Persistence is justified only when measured rebuild and startup costs exceed the accepted envelope.

## Alternatives Considered

1. Explicit in-memory rebuild on demand.
2. Versioned opaque chunks or internal tables in the Turso file.
3. A derived sidecar only after an explicit change to the one-file product contract.
acceptance_criteria: Chosen mode is evidence-backed; crash/build/publish/stale/schema/corruption tests prove derived state is discardable and canonical rows remain unchanged.
